name: Arcturus Defense Solutions CrisisNet BT-4 Battlefield Triage
description:
The CrisisNet BT-4 is Arcturus Defense Solutions' advanced battlefield triage and medical coordination BCI, engineered for combat medics and field surgeons operating in high-lethality environments where conventional diagnostic tools are unavailable or impractical. The device maintains simultaneous biometric uplinks to up to sixteen casualty monitoring nodes—wearable sensors distributed among squad members—processing vital sign data, wound classification algorithms, and pharmaceutical interaction flags in real time and rendering this information as a color-coded triage overlay within the operator's visual field. Its four-stream processing architecture handles concurrent casualty prioritization, medical supply inventory tracking, medevac coordination communications, and direct neural-assisted surgical guidance simultaneously, with an integrated haptic feedback system that guides the operator's hands through complex field procedures via precise motor cortex stimulation. The BT-4's comms stack is quantum-encrypted and ADS-standard EMP hardened, ensuring medical data integrity even in contested electromagnetic environments where enemy jamming is active.

The CrisisNet BT-4 has earned a reputation among combat medics in Meridian 88's military as the device that has genuinely shifted survival rates in high-intensity engagements—internal ADS studies (selectively disclosed) claim a 34% improvement in field triage accuracy and a 28% reduction in preventable battlefield deaths among units equipped with BT-4 operators. This statistical weight has given CrisisNet medics an almost talismanic status in the units they serve; soldiers who have been 'pulled back' by a BT-4 operator speak of the experience with a specific reverence, describing the operator's preternatural calm and the uncanny precision of their movements during crisis intervention. The device's haptic surgical guidance system has also attracted interest from civilian trauma surgery communities, and Arcturus has faced persistent lobbying pressure to release a stripped civilian variant—pressure the company has so far resisted on grounds of proprietary military advantage.
installation_requirements: Tier 4 certified neurosurgeon; medical operator license required; ADS BioLink Compatibility Assessment; 10-day post-installation calibration with live biometric node testing; haptic motor cortex mapping procedure (separate 4-hour session)
maintenance: Monthly biometric node protocol sync; haptic motor mapping recalibration every 6 months; pharmaceutical database updates pushed via ADS secure uplink quarterly; annual full system diagnostic
specifications: {"simultaneous_casualty_links": 16, "data_streams": 4, "triage_overlay_refresh": "120Hz", "haptic_guidance": "Motor cortex stimulation, precision ±0.3mm", "biometric_parameters_monitored": ["Heart rate", "Blood pressure", "O2 saturation", "Neurological activity", "Hemorrhage detection", "Pharmaceutical levels"], "comms": "Quantum-encrypted medevac coordination", "emp_hardening": "Class III ADS standard", "supply_tracking": "Real-time inventory overlay", "power_source": "Bio-electric primary, 36hr reserve", "weight": "31g installed", "tier": 4}
side_effects: Involuntary triage assessment of individuals in non-combat social environments—operators unconsciously monitor biometrics of nearby people, which can surface as intrusive awareness of others' physiological states
Haptic guidance system occasionally generates phantom surgical motion impulses during REM sleep, causing minor repetitive hand movements
Emotional blunting during crisis events as the BT-4's cognitive load management suppresses affective responses—some operators report difficulty re-engaging normal emotional processing post-engagement
Rare: motor cortex haptic mapping conflicts with fine motor tasks unrelated to medical procedures, causing temporary degraded dexterity in affected movement domains
cultural_context: BT-4 operators are among the most protected individuals in any unit they serve—soldiers have been documented taking extraordinary tactical risks to keep their CrisisNet medic alive and operational, a behavioral pattern that ADS's recruitment materials quietly reference without explicitly naming. In Meridian 88's veteran communities, the phrase 'had a Net' is shorthand for acknowledging that a unit had access to a level of field medical capability that genuinely changed outcomes, and veterans who served without one speak of it as a defining privation.
known_users: Meridian 88 Military Medical Corps elite units
story_hooks: A BT-4 operator's casualty monitoring logs contain biometric data from an engagement that officially never happened—including the vital signs of individuals who are officially listed as having died in a completely different incident.

The haptic surgical guidance database has been compromised: someone has injected false procedure guidance into the pharmaceutical interaction flags, and at least one field medic has already administered a lethal combination following the corrupted instructions.

A retired BT-4 operator is being blackmailed with triage data their device recorded during a classified operation—data that proves war crimes were committed by individuals now in prominent civilian positions.
